scenario: AITA for not hosting thanksgiving like I planned to | For about 50 years, my mom hosted all of her children and grandchildren for thanksgiving and Christmas Eve. She’s now gotten too old and asked us kids to take over the tradition. There are 4 of us so we just rotate. We’ve each hosted one holiday so far. This thanksgiving is my turn. We have never spent thanksgiving or Christmas Eve with my wife’s family. We’ve just never been as close to them plus they live all over the country. Well this year her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy’s thanksgiving day parade. At first it was just a sister’s trip but then they decided to invite all their kids and grandkids to meet them up there. My wife really wants to go. She hasnt seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter wants to go because it’s a “once in a lifetime event” (which i agree with). And I want to go. As soon as we decided to go I called my older brother to see what we should do about thanksgiving because I can’t host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and i have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I call her and she is mad. She says she’ll probably have to end up hosting even though she is up next for Christmas and I’m being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. “Mom wouldn’t abandon thanksgiving to go to nyc” and went on about how sad mom will be that I’m doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered but she said that takes away from the close knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it but he didn’t sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can’t do it because she’s renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn but I tried to offer up solutions and I also offered to host the next holiday—which my oldest sister said no to because it’s her turn and she’s been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother so I said me and him could maybe just swap thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm in the wrong here. Let me start by understanding the situation. My mom has been hosting Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve for about 50 years, and now she's too old, so we, her four kids, are supposed to take over the tradition by rotating. Each of us has hosted one holiday so far. This year, it's my turn to host Thanksgiving. But here's the thing: my wife's family has never been close, and they live all over the country. This year, her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade. At first, it was just a sister trip, but then they invited all their kids and grandkids to meet them there. My wife really wants to go because she hasn't seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter also wants to go because it's a once-in-a-lifetime event, and I agree with that. Plus, I want to go too. So, as soon as we decided to go, I called my older brother to figure out what we should do about Thanksgiving since I can't host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and that I have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I called her, and she was mad. She said she'll probably have to end up hosting even though it's her turn for Christmas, and I'm being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. She also mentioned that Mom wouldn't abandon Thanksgiving to go to New York and went on about how sad Mom will be that I'm doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered, but she said that takes away from the close-knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it, but he didn't sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can't do it because she's renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn, but I tried to offer solutions and also offered to host the next holiday, which my oldest sister said no to because it's her turn and she's been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother, so I said me and him could maybe just swap Thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here? I'm not sure. On one hand, I want to spend Thanksgiving with my wife's family, and it seems like a special opportunity. On the other hand, I'm supposed to be hosting Thanksgiving this year as part of the rotation we agreed on with my siblings. My oldest sister is upset, and my brother isn't too happy about it either. I tried to come up with solutions, like paying for someone else to host or swapping with my brother, but it doesn't seem like that's working out. I guess I'm wondering if it's okay to prioritize my own family's wishes over the tradition we've been following. Is it wrong to back out of hosting Thanksgiving because I want to do something else? Or is it more important to stick to the plan we made to honor our mom's tradition? I also feel like I'm letting my siblings down, especially my oldest sister who is upset and feels like she's being forced to host again. Maybe I should have communicated better with my siblings earlier or tried to find a compromise that works for everyone. But I'm not sure what else I could have done. I offered to pay for someone else to host, but that didn't go over well. Maybe I should have been more understanding of how important this tradition is to my siblings and our mom, even if it's not as important to my wife's family. I'm also thinking about the bigger picture. Is this one Thanksgiving worth potentially damaging relationships with my siblings? Or is it worth it to create a new tradition with my wife's family? I don't want to be the one who breaks the tradition, but I also don't want to miss out on this special opportunity with my wife and daughter. I guess I'm torn between honoring the commitment I made to my siblings and pursuing something that's important to my own family. I'm not sure which side is more right or wrong. Maybe there's a middle ground I haven't considered yet, like finding a way to include both families or adjusting the plans in a way that works for everyone. But at this point, it seems like things are pretty set in stone, and I'm not sure how to move forward without upsetting someone. Overall, I'm feeling conflicted about whether I'm in the wrong for wanting to go to the parade instead of hosting Thanksgiving. I understand why my siblings are upset, but I also feel like this is a meaningful opportunity for my own family. I wish there was a way to make everyone happy, but I'm not sure if that's possible in this situation.
